context: Real construction from Q: nonempty proper lower set without greatest element
display_term: Dedekind cut of the rational numbers
editorial_screening_reason: PlanetMath's four conditions each have a precise logical role. Nonempty and proper exclude endpoints at negative and positive infinity; downward closure fixes the lower-set convention, while having no largest rational selects the unique lower side at each rational boundary. This is different from a Dedekind-complete abstract ordered set.

formulations.text: A (lower) Dedekind cut of the rational numbers is a subset A of Q such that A is nonempty, A is not all of Q, if a belongs to A then every rational q<a also belongs to A, and A has no largest element.

context: Concrete Dedekind-cut realization: real numbers represented by rational lower cuts
editorial_screening_reason: PlanetMath defines real numbers in this model as the rational cuts themselves and orders distinct cuts by strict inclusion. The non-strict relation is its reflexive extension. The rational embedding via strict lower rays is injection preserving order. The claim that arithmetic and completeness hold is an additional proof obligation, not a substitution for those proofs. The new model is a contextual real-number definition, not literal equality to the abstract axiomatic complete ordered field.

formulations.text: In the Dedekind-cut construction, the underlying set R_D consists of all lower Dedekind cuts A of Q. Define the order by A≤B if and only if A⊆B. Each rational q has the canonical representation {r∈Q:r<q}. Defining arithmetic on cuts and proving the ordered-field axioms and the least-upper-bound property then gives a concrete realization of a real-number system.
